sentences.text: Peipehsuchus is an extinct genus of teleosaurid crocodyliform.
The type specimen, which is the specific fossil the species is based on, consists only of a fragmentary rostrum and teeth.
A complete teleosaurid skull was once assigned to Peipehsuchus, but it was later determined that the skull does not belong to the genus because the type specimen is a metriorhynchoid.
Peipehsuchus is classified within the family Teleosauridae.
It belongs to the suborder Thalattosuchia.

Peipehsuchus was originally considered a member of the family Pholidosauridae according to Steel in 1973, but later analyses showed its affinities with teleosaurids, a suggestion first made by Buffeteaut in 1982 and confirmed by Li in 1993.
Peipehsuchus lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the Toarcian age.
The time range for Peipehsuchus is the Callovian, from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
Fossils of the type species P. teleorhinus have been found in China and fragmentary remains in the Callovian of Kyrgyzstan.
Peipehsuchus was part of a group of crocodiles similar to gharials that showed a tendency toward adaptation to aquatic life.
